slides.texte_overlay:
Things that make you
quietly impressive
Know how to tie a tie without a video. A four-in-hand takes ten seconds once you've practiced. The day a friend panics before his wedding and you fix it in a minute, you'll understand why.
Know how to change a tire. Jack, spare, wheel nuts in a star pattern. Twenty minutes on the side of the road, calmly, while everyone else is googling. Nobody forgets that kind of calm.
Carry a little cash and a pen. Old school, sure. But when the card machine is down or someone needs to write down a number, you're the guy who has it. Tiny thing, quietly impressive.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. You won't announce it. People will just notice you always seem to know the story behind things.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. You won't announce it. People will just notice you always know the story behind things.

slides.texte_overlay: Know how to cook one dish really well. Not ten. One. A great carbonara, a perfect steak, a real curry. Make it for people you like. Being known for one thing beats being average at everything.
Know your way without GPS in your own city. Main streets, shortcuts, a few good places to eat. When the phone dies, you're the one who still knows exactly where to go and how to get there.
Keep a small kit in your bag. Plasters, painkillers, a charger, gum. You'll be surprised how often someone needs one of them, and how much they remember the guy who quietly had it ready.
